rows.n: target IDs
rows.b: The token IDs the model is supposed to predict — the answers for its input IDs.

rows.n: teacher forcing
rows.b: Feeding the model the true previous tokens during training instead of its own guesses, which stabilizes learning.

rows.n: temperature
rows.b: A dial on randomness: low values make the model pick the most likely token, high values make it more creative and surprising.

rows.n: test set
rows.b: The locked-away questions used for final scoring, never seen during training.

rows.n: text normalization
rows.b: Standardizing text before tokenizing, like unifying quotes or unicode forms.

rows.n: throughput
rows.b: How many tokens the system can generate per second across all users.

rows.n: tied embeddings
rows.b: Reusing the same matrix for input embeddings and the output projection, saving parameters.

rows.n: time to first token
rows.b: How quickly the first token appears after a request — what makes a chat feel snappy or sluggish.

rows.n: token budget
rows.b: The total number of tokens a training run will process — the main dial controlling cost and quality.

rows.n: token embedding
rows.b: The embedding looked up for each input token before the model starts processing the sequence.

rows.n: token ID
rows.b: The number standing in for a token inside the model — text becomes lists of IDs before any math happens.

rows.n: token streaming
rows.b: Sending each generated token to the user the moment it is produced, instead of waiting for the whole answer.

rows.n: tokenization
rows.b: The act of splitting text into tokens — the first step of everything a language model does.

rows.n: tokenizer
rows.b: The tool that chops raw text into tokens before the model sees it, and turns tokens back into text afterward.

rows.n: tool use
rows.b: The broader ability of a model to operate external tools — search, calculators, code runners — during a conversation.

rows.n: top-k sampling
rows.b: Only letting the model choose among the k most likely next tokens, cutting off the weird tail of the distribution.

rows.n: top-p sampling
rows.b: Nucleus sampling: choosing from the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities add up to p, adapting to the model's confidence.

rows.n: toxicity
rows.b: Measuring how often a model produces hateful, abusive, or otherwise harmful text.

rows.n: TPU
rows.b: Google's tensor processing unit, a custom chip designed for massive-scale training.

rows.n: training
rows.b: The process of feeding a model huge amounts of text and adjusting its parameters until it predicts language well.

rows.n: training corpus
rows.b: The full collection of text a model learns from; Signature Llama's is the Signature Dictionary plus the Signature spec archive.

rows.n: training data
rows.b: The actual text the model learns from during training.

rows.n: transformer
rows.b: The neural network design behind modern language models, built from stacked blocks that weigh how every word relates to every other word.

rows.n: transformer block
rows.b: One repeating unit of the model: attention, then a feed-forward network, each wrapped with normalization and residuals.

rows.n: truncation
rows.b: Cutting a sequence down to the maximum length the model accepts.

rows.n: TruthfulQA
rows.b: A test of whether the model repeats common myths or tells the truth about tricky questions.
